study_identification_part.si4_title: Heterogeneity of morphometric similarity networks in health and schizophrenia

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the study aims: apply longitudinal normative modeling to morphometric similarity to assess whether decreases are consistent across individuals with schizophrenia, quantify individual deviations over time, and evaluate clinical relevance. This satisfies: (1) research questions/hypotheses are provided, and (2) the purpose of applying normative modeling is described (to assess heterogeneity, identify deviations, and compare SZ vs controls).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "…employing longitudinal normative modeling to evaluate whether decreases are consistent across individuals with schizophrenia. Normative models were trained and validated… Individual deviations… were measured at baseline and follow-up…"; "In this study, we apply normative modeling to morphometric similarity… to parse both the cross-sectional and longitudinal heterogeneity…"

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Reference cohort (healthy individuals) comes from ten public datasets plus healthy controls from a clinical dataset. The sources are cited; image quality criteria are specified via FreeSurfer Euler number threshold and extensive QC; exclusions are reported (29 subjects removed); final training/test sample sizes are given. This meets all criteria for newly built models: eligibility/data sources cited, QC specified, and final sample sizes/exclusions reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We included healthy participants from ten publicly available datasets…"; "All T1-weighted images… processed… FreeSurfer (v7.1)… Freesurfer Euler number… Subjects were removed if… larger than 10, and 29 subjects were removed."; "The training set included 4310 participants and the test set 859 participants."
